description: Intraday. Sells an ATM straddle with 1.5% wings only in the last two calendar days before NIFTY's weekly expiry, after 09:45, while the index is still inside its opening range and VIX is not rising. Intraday because the edge is same-day theta, and wings plus a tight stop cap the worst day.
hypothesis: Near expiry, ATM theta is a large share of the premium within one session. The textbook straddle loses on trend days. Entering only once the first 30 minutes stay inside a range and VIX is flat should skip most trend days and keep the decay. Wings cap gap risk, and the stop is set near the target so costs do not eat the edge. BANKNIFTY's monthly expiry makes it mostly idle, so this is designed for NIFTY. Honest expectation is 1-3% a month, not 5-7%.
lessons: Selling 0-3 DTE premium when IV rank is low and the market is sideways gives no edge: the premium is too cheap to pay for the intraday tail moves. Undefined or loosely defined risk near expiry produces single days of -10% to -20%, which fails the pass rule on its own. Size positions to the actual capital and pick strikes that exist in the chain, or the backtest only describes a few days. A filter on mid IV rank or trend would cut trading to a few times a year, which fails the frequency aim. The next idea needs a hard daily loss cap built in and must enter on most sessions.

why_failed: Fails on both indexes. Worst day was -13.7% on NIFTY and -20.3% on BANKNIFTY, against a -10% limit. Drawdowns were 58% and 43%. The average month was -4.0% (NIFTY) and -2.4% (BANKNIFTY), far from the 5-7% target. Only 36-43% of months were positive. 2024 lost -57% and -47% while holding lost about -6%. edge_t was negative (-1.42, -1.03), so there is no edge at all, not just bad luck. The losses sit in the bulk of trades: sideways trend, normal VIX (13-18) and low IV rank. Each of those was most of the trades and most of the loss. Entry was mostly blocked: NIFTY hit 'not enough capital' 1472 times, BANKNIFTY had 'no strike' on 132 sessions. So sizing and strike selection don't match the capital or the chain.
why_worked: Very little. 2025 was roughly flat on NIFTY (+0.9%) and matched holding on BANKNIFTY (+13.7% vs +13.5%). Trades entered at middle-third IV rank won 87% (NIFTY, 8 trades) and 83% (BANKNIFTY, 6 trades). Trades in trending markets, rising or falling, were positive on both indexes. These subsets are 3-20 trades each, too small to trust, and would trade only a few times a year.

description: Intraday. Sells a near-expiry ATM put spread only after the index trades above its open while VIX falls, and closes it the same day. It is intraday because it needs about 15 decision days a month to pass the 10-trades rule, and because it avoids overnight gaps, which killed every positional seller in the atlas. NIFTY weeklies give the theta; on BANKNIFTY's monthly expiry the edge is mainly skew.
hypothesis: Index puts carry a skew premium: buyers overpay for crash cover. On a day when the index holds above its open and VIX is falling, intraday put demand fades and ATM put IV bleeds, while the drift tends to persist. A defined-risk spread with a stop caps the worst day near 5%. Selling only on confirmed-strength days, not every day, is what sets it apart from the atlas straddles. Honestly this likely earns 1-3% a month, not 5-7%. Reaching 5-7% would need more margin than the -10% worst-day limit allows.
lessons: The core entry loses most in its most common condition: sideways, low IV rank, normal VIX. It is not a filtering problem that one rule change can fix. Single-day losses of 7-9% show the risk per trade is too large for a 30% drawdown limit. Strike selection must be robust on BANKNIFTY (expiry and strike-grid changes) or most sessions are skipped. Positive slices with 3-22 trades should not be chased; that is overfitting.

why_failed: Both indexes fail. NIFTY loses 1.14% a month on average, is positive in only 43% of months, has a 27.6% fall from its high and a worst day of -9.1%, and edge_t is -0.7, which is no edge. BANKNIFTY also skipped 64% of sessions (147 'no strike'), so the rules as written cannot be entered on most days. Losses cluster in sideways, low-IV, normal-VIX entries, which is where nearly all trades happen.
why_worked: Very little worked. NIFTY's 2025 beat holding (+12.4% vs +9.0%) but followed a -28% 2024. Entries 4-7 days to expiry were positive on both indexes (NIFTY 22 trades, +0.19% average; BANKNIFTY 11 trades, +2.0% average). NIFTY falling-trend entries were positive (10 trades). description: Intraday. Near expiry, sell an ATM put spread on days the index breaks above its opening range while VIX falls. The intraday mode gives real minute fills, tight stops with no overnight gaps, and the fast theta of the last 3 days. The defined-risk wing keeps margin small enough to open sets in 2025-26.
hypothesis: Index puts carry a skew premium, and on strong mornings with falling VIX that put premium decays fastest near expiry. Requiring breakout plus falling VIX filters out the trend-down days that killed the plain sellers. The wing and a 60% stop cap a bad day near -6%. Honestly, this likely earns 1-3% a month, not 5-7%. It may also trade under 10 times a month on BANKNIFTY, which has only a monthly expiry.
lessons: Taking near-expiry trades whenever IV is low and the market is sideways has a reliably negative edge on both indexes. The edge appears only when premium is rich, and that happens too rarely to reach the trade count needed for 5-7% a month. Filtering down to those few trades would make the version fail on trade frequency. With a significantly negative edge_t after three versions, more tuning is unlikely to help. The next idea should have its edge on ordinary days, should cap daily loss by design (for example defined-risk structures), and should avoid strikes that BANKNIFTY often lacks.

entry.when: dte <= 3 and not event_today and close > or_high and close > day_open and vix_chg_pct < 0 and vix < 22

title: Intraday bull put spread on opening-range breakouts near expiry
why_failed: Both indexes fail the pass rule. NIFTY fell 49.5% from its high (limit 30%), averaged -4.46% a month, was positive in only 14% of months, and had an edge_t of -2.46. That t-value is significantly negative, so the losses are not bad luck. BANKNIFTY's worst day was -11.8% (limit -10%), it fell 31% and averaged -2.36% a month at only 1.1 trades a month, and 26% of its sessions were skipped for having no strike. Holding beat the strategy in every year on both indexes: NIFTY 2025 was -15.6% against +9.0%, BANKNIFTY 2025 -5.9% against +13.5%. Nearly every trade was entered 0-3 days before expiry with IV rank in the low third, and those trades lose about 1.2-2.8% each. The worst days run -6% to -12%, so the losses are large and come in bursts.
why_worked: Very little worked. The few trades entered when VIX was above 18 or IV rank was in the middle third made money (NIFTY 1 trade, BANKNIFTY 2+2). Falling-trend entries on NIFTY were roughly flat. These samples are tiny, so they hint at a direction and prove nothing. They suggest the idea only pays when option prices are rich, and the cheap, low-IV, near-expiry setups make up most of the trades and lose.

description: Intraday. Near expiry (dte <= 3), a weekly option's remaining time value decays sharply within one session, so the theta is worth collecting the same day. Intraday also avoids the overnight gaps that broke the positional sellers. The defined-risk wings keep margin small, so 2025-26 sets can be bought, and they cap the worst minute.
hypothesis: Near expiry, NIFTY weekly premium decays fast inside a day. On days when the index stays inside its 09:15-09:44 range and VIX is not rising, realised movement tends to fall short of implied, so a 20-delta condor kept to the afternoon should earn its decay after costs. The textbook iron fly sat at the money and traded every day; this one avoids trend and vol-spike days. Honestly, 5-7% a month is unlikely: I expect roughly 1-3%. BANKNIFTY's monthly expiry will rarely qualify.
lessons: A high win rate does not survive one uncapped tail day. Each index's failure traces to one or two sessions, so a hard intraday loss cap is the binding constraint. A 0-3 day expiry filter starves BANKNIFTY of trades now that its weekly expiries are gone, and strike lookup fails on most days. That frequency problem is structural and one tweak will not fix it. NIFTY's edge is only noise, and the conditional splits are too thin to filter on without overfitting.

title: Near-expiry inside-range iron condor (NIFTY weekly)

indexes.warning: skipped on 59% of sessions (132 no strike, 24 no minute data): most days the strategy could not be entered as written, so these numbers describe very few days

why_failed: Both indexes fail the worst-day rule: NIFTY -13.9% on 2025-05-12 and BANKNIFTY -11.2% on 2024-10-22 (that same day cost NIFTY -10.4%), so one bad session sinks a month. NIFTY has no real edge. Edge_t is 0.39, only 50% of months are positive and the average is 1.08%, far below 5-7%. Its profit comes from 47 rising-trend or calm/fearful-VIX trades, while the 99 normal-VIX and 98 sideways trades lose money. BANKNIFTY carries a warning: 59% of sessions were skipped (132 no strike), leaving 2.36 trades a month and 33 trades in total. Its 6% average month rests on very few days.
why_worked: The core intraday near-expiry trade has a high win rate (69% NIFTY, 82% BANKNIFTY) and beat holding in every year on both indexes. On BANKNIFTY, the days it could enter were strongly profitable across every VIX and trend bucket. Edge_t is 2.04, so the result is unlikely to be pure luck. Apart from one outlier day, BANKNIFTY's losing days were small: the next worst was -1.96%, and the worst fall was 0.96%.
